arxiv-2209-10402.title: classical circuits can simulate quantum aspects
arxiv-2209-10402.creator: M. Caruso
arxiv-2209-10402.description: Abstract This study introduces a method for simulating quantum systems using electrical networks. Our approach leverages a generalized similarity transformation, which connects different Hamiltonians, enabling well-defined paths for quantum system simulation using classical circuits. By synthesizing interaction networks, we accurately simulate quantum systems of varying complexity, from 2 − 2- state to n − n- state systems.

arxiv-2212-10042.title: Guarantees for Comprehensive Simulation Assessment of Statistical Methods
arxiv-2212-10042.creator: James Yang, T. Ben Thompson, Michael Sklar
arxiv-2212-10042.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by James Yang, T. Ben Thompson, Michael Sklar. Simulation can evaluate a statistical method for properties such as Type I Error, FDR, or bias on a grid of hypothesized parameter values. But what about the gaps between the grid-points? Continuous Simulation Extension (CSE) is a proof-by-simulation framework which can supplement simulations with (1) confidence bands valid over regions of parameter space or (2) calibration of rejection thresholds to provide rigorous proof of strong Type I Error control.

arxiv-2505-01128.description: Abstract We study the full time-domain evolution of gravitational perturbations in black hole spacetimes arising in Einstein–Weyl gravity, a renormalizable extension of general relativity containing quadratic curvature corrections.
